Furthest from his ghost

    Each defender is judged on his own, with his teammates where they really were.

    How it works

    The idea comes from pro analytics, where it is called ghosting. Coaches use it to ask whether a goal was bad luck or bad positioning.

    Watch

    The model studied thousands of moments from 23 pro matches. Three were tracked in the stadium. Twenty were tracked from the normal TV broadcast, where only part of the pitch is on screen.

    Hide and guess

    In training we hide a defender and ask: he stood here a few seconds ago, the play went like this, where is he now? The model guesses. We show it the truth. Repeat many times.

    Compare

    On a new goal, the guess is the ghost. A defender far from his ghost did something an average pro would not have done. That is where to look first.

    Does it work?

    Every number below is from a match the model had never seen. The 23 matches were split into 4 groups. The model was trained 4 times, each time with one group left out, and tested on the group it did not see.

    How far the ghost lands from where the real defender went

    Average miss in meters. Lower is better. Whole defense hidden.

    What it cannot do yet

    Read these before trusting a ghost.

    • It learned from 23 matches. That is still little. Clubs train this kind of model on hundreds. More data would make the ghosts sharper.
    • A ghost is the average pro, not the perfect one. Far from the ghost means unusual. It does not always mean wrong. A press or an offside trap looks unusual too.
    • It was trained on open play. Corners and free kicks are a different game. The page marks goals that start from a corner.
    • It does not find players in video. The matches and goals here were tracked from TV by other people (SkillCorner and Last Row). My own camera stage is tested with a pretend camera, not real footage.
    • The goal clips are rough. Their makers say the tracking was built for animations. Small distances in those clips mean little.
    • The danger score is simple. It only asks who reaches each spot first. It knows nothing about the ball, passing lanes or who the striker is.
    Data: Metrica Sports sample data and SkillCorner open data for training and testing. Last Row (Ricardo Tavares) for the 19 Liverpool goals tracked from TV.
    Ideas: ghosting from Le, Carr, Yue and Lucey (2017). Space control from Spearman (2018).
